clue.text: Guy — idle cur I trounced

indicators.note: trounced means thoroughly beaten up, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a lazy mongrel after beating it soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man's name but is the verb: to guy someone is to mock them. 'trounced' rearranges IDLECURI.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old verb for mocking or poking fun at them, which is what ridicule does.

clue.text: Erect, I go out to make a prepared statement

indicators.note: go out suggests the letters break ranks and form up in another order

explanation.surface: A man stands up and walks out to deliver a scripted speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' rearranges ERECTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to speak from memory something learned in advance.

clue.text: Put into shape and stop

definitions.meaning: to arrange or draft, as one does a plan
to halt, as a vehicle does at the kerb

explanation.definitionFit: To draft a document is to give it form, and a carriage pulls in and halts.

clue.text: Conspire to get old king to receive lord

indicators.note: to receive means the king takes the lord inside himself

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of a nursery rhyme
lud is the old form of lord, as in a barrister's m'lud

explanation.surface: A plot to have an ancient monarch welcome a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: COLE is Old King Cole from the English nursery rhyme; LUD is 'lord' as said in court ('m'lud'). 'to receive' puts LUD inside COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To collude is to plot secretly with others, to scheme together.

clue.text: Secure some hair

explanation.definitionFit: A key fastens a door, and a tress is a small curl of one's hair.

clue.text: Duck given to the Queen by British national

parts.note: a Scot is a national of Scotland, part of Britain
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A bird is presented to the monarch by a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea bird of the waterfowl family, a kind of diving sea fowl.

clue.text: Sycophantic plant?

parts.note: a fawning toady and a vine or ivy that crawls up a wall both go by the same name, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A fawning shrub is imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady who sucks up is a crawler, and so is a climbing or trailing vine.

clue.text: Got there possibly at the same time

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of the ways these letters could be arranged

explanation.surface: Two people may manage to arrive simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text reads 'Get', but only GOT THERE has the letters; 'possibly' rearranges GOTTHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that happen jointly happen simultaneously.

clue.text: Showing no mercy, though girl smaller

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: Someone is pitiless, even though the girl is little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means pitiless, ruth being an old word for pity.

clue.text: Plant fish by river barrier

parts.note: the char is a trout-like freshwater fish
a lock is a gated section that holds back water on a river or canal

explanation.surface: An angler sets down a catch beside a weir on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb (put the fish down) but is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a yellow-flowered weed of fields.

clue.text: Everest leader badly strained thigh circling summit

indicators.note: circling means the jumbled thigh letters go round the other piece
badly strained suggests the thigh muscle is pulled out of shape, so its letters are jumbled
the leader of the word Everest is its first letter

explanation.surface: A climber at the front on Everest has pulled a thigh muscle near the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly strained' turns THIGH into HIGHT, and 'circling' wraps it round E, the first letter of Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: A height is a high point or peak, so it stands for a summit.

clue.text: Leave-surrounded by bird song from the palm tree

indicators.note: surrounded by means the leaving word is enclosed by the bird song

parts.note: coo is the soft call of a dove or pigeon
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: A tree among leaves, ringed by the song of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts QUIT inside COO; 'from the' only links. 'Leave' reads as foliage but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The coquito is the Chilean wine palm, a tall South American species.

clue.text: Bull moving back at us, crossing old city

indicators.note: crossing means the other pieces straddle the old city, which sits between them
moving back says the little word at is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
taken as written
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A charging bull backs towards us across an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving back' turns AT into TA; TA and US straddle UR, the ancient Sumerian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is the zodiac sign and constellation of the bull, its Latin name.

clue.text: A lot wrong. with hips? Here's the solution

indicators.note: wrong suggests something is out of place, so these letters are put right in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose hips are giving lots of trouble is told where the cure lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ALOT and HIPS. The definition is playful: for bad hips, the answer is where the fix happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of medical treatment is where bad hips get replaced, so it is the remedy for the trouble described.

clue.text: Not in favour of smashing red vase

indicators.note: smashing breaks the vase to pieces, so its letters and those of red are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone opposes breaking a red pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges REDVASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or opposed, against something.

clue.text: The rear squad travelling to base

indicators.note: travelling means these letters are on the move into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A rearguard unit makes its way back to camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges THEREARSQUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A military base is the central command post, the head office of an operation.

clue.text: Travelling abroad the French are charming

indicators.note: travelling sets the letters of abroad moving into a new order

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Touring overseas, the French are delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' rearranges ABROAD into ADORAB; LE (French 'the') follows. 'are' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is lovable and delightful.

clue.text: Mixed doubles — second fault -—not disheartened, he aims high

annotationWithheld.why: Mixed doubles — second fault -—not disheartened, he aims high (8) for ASPIRANT: PAIRS anagram gives ASPIR, but no reading of 'second fault — not disheartened' gives ANT; OCR or setter garble not resolved by search.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mixed doubles — second fault -—not disheartened, he aims high

clue.text: Can't find site for recycling germ-killer

indicators.note: for recycling says these letters are processed and made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone with a used bleach bottle can't locate the recycling depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for recycling' rearranges CANTFINDSITE; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A disinfectant is a chemical cleaner that destroys bacteria.

clue.text: Oven turned out everything cooked —- that's the tale

indicators.note: turned out means the oven's letters are tipped into a new order
cooked suggests the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A chef empties the oven, everything done, and that's the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' gives NOVE from OVEN and 'cooked' gives LLA from ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a story longer than a short story.

clue.text: Fully in order to cancel

indicators.note: order means the letters are put into a sequence different from the printed one

explanation.surface: Fully in order to call it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges FULLYIN; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to make void, invalidating something.

clue.text: Town looted in a disturbance

indicators.note: in a disturbance suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A place was ransacked during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a disturbance' rearranges LOOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic Spanish city (and one in Ohio).

clue.text: Hear why a slum provides refuge

indicators.note: provides is read as the slum making room for that letter within itself

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Hear says the word why is said out loud, sounding like a letter

parts.note: said out loud, why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: The question why a slum gives sanctuary is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' turns WHY into the letter Y, which A SLUM makes room for ('provides').
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection and safety granted to those fleeing danger.

clue.text: Once again, ceremoniously clothe soldiers in underwear

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are a British army corps
taken as written
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Troops in their undershirts are dressed again in ceremonial robes.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword soldiers; VEST in Britain is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to robe them formally on taking office, and the prefix makes it a repeat.

clue.text: Knocks down more than one storey

definitions.meaning: a boxer knocks an opponent to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer who fells an opponent decks them, and a building's levels are also its stages.

clue.text: One's not enough to show approval

definitions.text: One's not enough to show approval

parts.words: One's not enough to show approval
parts.note: the cry of assent in Parliament is one word said twice, so a single one falls short

explanation.surface: A single cheer won't do to show support.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs in the British House of Commons signal agreement by calling 'hear, hear!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubled, it is the shout of agreement from British parliamentary benches.

clue.text: Insect circling agitated lad and official in synagogue

indicators.note: circling means the insect's letters go round the stirred-up lad

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of lad are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A bee buzzes round an upset boy and a synagogue officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns LAD into ADL, which 'circling' puts inside BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a lay officer; in a synagogue the term names the caretaker or sexton (shammes).

clue.text: Peer in a lap-top, repositioning this gland

indicators.note: repositioning means the letters are moved into new places
the top of lap is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a laptop computer while shifting a medical image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repositioning' rearranges PEERINA into PERINEA; L, the top of 'lap-top', ends it. The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective, as in a gland of the perineum.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a gland of the perineum, the region between the anus and genitals.

clue.text: Catch spouse turning tail —- right away!

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is removed
turning tail suggests running back the way one came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a partner is a husband or wife

explanation.surface: Catch your husband running off, and quick about it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' turns PARTNER into RENTRAP; 'away' drops its first R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them by a trick.

clue.text: Military women or men chasing a caterpillar

parts.note: the army is the military
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for men or male

explanation.surface: Servicewomen or servicemen pursue a crawling insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' only joins the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The armyworm is a moth larva that moves through crops in great hordes, a destructive grub.
